name: Shell City Landing Campground - Huntersville State Forest
note: Rustic DNR state-forest campground in a red-pine stand at the Shell City canoe landing on the Shell River, a short paddle above the Crow Wing River water trail, between Menahga and Nimrod; managed by Itasca State Park. The DNR posts no site length, so pad size is unconfirmed. The separate Shell City horse camp lies in an open clearing about 350 m east. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: MN DNR Compass feature record sft00025 (last_updated 2026-06-09, read 2026-11-12): facility cmp00027 'Shell City Landing Campground', camping campsites 19, fee 1, toilets 2, wells 1, 'primitive ... cleared area, fire ring, table, vault toilets, garbage cans, and drinking water', on the Shell River; a separate facility cmp00058 'Shell City Horse Campground' (horse_campsites 8, tie lines/corrals/stalls). DNR forest map (2017-18 PDF, scale 126.5 pt/mi) draws 'Shell City Campground' (tent + canoe-campsite icons, own toilet and water) at the landing and a separate horse-camp symbol with its own toilet/water ~27 pt (~340 m) east; Esri Wayback 2011-05-15 leaf-off aerial shows a gravel loop with spurs in the pine stand at the landing, distinct from the open horse clearing at ~46.7918,-94.9430 (trailers parked, 2015-04-18 frame shows its building). Explore Minnesota profile 2896: 19 sites, FCFS, phone 218-699-7251; Campendium: last nightly rate $17. The Dyrt (only review, 2018-11-16, visit not a stay): sign says RVs welcome at the tent price, no hookups. -> a separate general drive-in state-forest campground, not the horse camp's loop (public: no price gate).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery (2024-03-20 WV02, rendered at 240 m/600 m via export and z19 3x3) and Esri Wayback 2011-05-15 UC-G 0.3 m leaf-off aerial (z18, rendered) plus 2015-04-18 GE01 (rendered). The campground sits under near-continuous red/jack pine (evergreen, so leaf-off frames don't open it); the 2011 aerial shows the loop's north spurs ending at clearings ~46.79197,-94.94805 and ~46.79227,-94.94768, the latter ~15-40 m from the water across an open sedge/marsh band (the band ~20 m wide on the 2024 frame, flooded on the May 2011 one); NE clearing ~46.79234,-94.94642 is the canoe landing (DNR map launch icon). Shell River main channel measured ~18-21 m wide on the z19 frame (46.7924,-94.9478) -> under the ~30 m line, so creekside would be the most on-water value. No site map (DNR cmp00027.pdf 404), sites unnumbered, and no frame shows which clearings are pads vs the landing/toilet, so no named site is placed within ~50 m over open ground: on-water not earned. View supported by the open marsh between the north spurs and the river and the only firsthand account (The Dyrt 2018-11-16: 'all pads within view of the river') -> riverview (same call as 5436 Huntersville Forest Landing on the Crow Wing). Not a reservoir; no dam.

fees.note: Minnesota state forest individual campsite, taxes included. Paid online on the arrival date or at a state park ranger station; nothing is collected at the campground. DNR state forest fee page, read 2026-11-12.

fees_source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html ('Individual and equestrian campsites $17 - $22'; 'Starting in 2026 ... $17 per night ($22 for equestrian)'; 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site'; 'Onsite staff cannot accept camping fee payments'), read 2026-11-12; Campendium 'Last nightly rate $17' (undated)

booking.note: First come; the fee is paid online on the day of arrival (or at a state park ranger station) before taking a site.

booking_source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/fees-reservations.html (same-day online payment for individual campsites: 'If you are not already at the campground, plan to arrive on the same day you made your payment ... choose an unoccupied campsite'; group sites only are reservable) + DNR facility cmp00027 (fee 1, no reservation link) + Explore Minnesota ('first come, first served'), read 2026-11-12
rvlife: none (RV Life 257448 'Shell City - Huntersville State Forest' sits at 46.739,-94.928 with 24 sites, i.e. it is 5436 Huntersville Forest Landing; no RV Life listing for this campground; read 2026-11-12)
flags: Horse-camp question resolved: DNR keeps two facilities (cmp00027 Landing, 19 general campsites, no horse amenities; cmp00058 Horse Campground, 8 horse sites); the 2017-18 forest map draws them ~340 m apart with separate toilet/water symbols, and imagery shows the pine loop at the landing vs the open horse clearing ~46.7918,-94.9430. Caveat: DNR's horse-camp point (46.791317,-94.946504) falls at the SE edge of the landing's pine stand, not on that clearing; DNR facility points look approximate. The 2017-18 guide text lists only 'Shell City Horse Campground ... eight individual campsites, 27 horse campsites' (19 + 8 = 27), so the landing may be the former horse-camp loop redesignated general; the current DNR record is what decides.

Rig fit: DNR, Explore Minnesota and Campendium give no length; the only review (The Dyrt 2018, no rig named) says the sign welcomes RVs and the road 'winds down a small path into the sites', AWD advisable in snow. Kept with the pad-size caveat (AWH 2026-11-02). No agency statement about a road problem.
Stay limit: Campendium quotes 14 days in summer, 21 days mid-September to early May (the DNR state forest rule); not read on a DNR page, so not stored.
Season: not stated by DNR (state forest lands open at all times); left absent. The Dyrt lists year-round.
Overpass (OSM) answered 406 to the request; treated as refused and not retried.
Duplicate check: nothing within 2 km in campgrounds.json; 5436 Huntersville Forest Landing is 6.1 km SSE (different campground); 5444 Shell City Horse Camp already removed.
